script_structures: No warmup — open directly on the strangest detail.
Say the wildest part first, everything else is just support.

Zero throat-clearing — first word is already the content.
Keep it to three short beats max.
State the surprising part first, explain second, exit third.
State the surprising claim first, then the one-line reason why.
State it, then immediately back it up with the 'why'.
Skip context entirely unless it's needed to land the punchline.
Structure it as claim, quick evidence, quick close.
Treat every sentence like it has to earn its place.
Front-load the payoff, spend the rest of the time justifying it.
One sentence of setup max, then the payoff.

Quick with a wink — this is fun, not frantic.

Urgent but controlled — fast doesn't mean sloppy.
Rapid cadence, but land the final word hard.
Matter-of-fact but fast, like reading a highlight reel.
Punch each key word slightly — cadence matters here.

Talk like you're genuinely in a hurry to tell someone.
Bright and quick, almost a little breathless.
Confident and quick, like you already know this lands.
